garmin.broadcast: Send power, cadence and speed to your Garmin
garmin.linked: {name} is paired with your phone through Garmin Connect. To use it as a sensor, disconnect it for a moment:
garmin.nameHint: While it's on, your phone's Bluetooth name is "Spindro"; switch it off and the old name comes back.
garmin.step2: On the Garmin: Sensors & Accessories → Add New → Power, then Speed/Cadence. Pick "Spindro".
garmin.step3: Start an Indoor Bike activity on the Garmin.
garmin.stuck: Garmin stuck on "Connecting"? If your watch is already paired with this phone through Garmin Connect, it often won't open a second connection. On the Garmin, turn off the phone connection for a moment (Settings → Connectivity → Phone), add the sensor, then turn it back on: the activity will sync when you finish.
garmin.unlinkBody: It's paired through Garmin Connect, so it can't pick up the "Spindro" sensor.
garmin.webOnly: Your phone can act as a sensor for your Garmin only in the Android app: download the APK.

home.unsupported: This browser can't do Bluetooth. On PC and Mac use Chrome or Edge; on Android use Chrome or the app; on iPhone use the Bluefy app.
music.hint: Long press (almost 1 second) on + = next track, on − = play / pause. A short press still shifts gear. Works with Spotify, YouTube Music, podcasts and any app playing in the background.
music.title: Music
music.webOnly: Available in the Android app: a browser can't control other apps.

plans.ritorno.desc: 4 weeks to restart after a break, no rush, with a test at the end.
plans.ritorno.name: Back in shape

video.drm: Netflix, Prime Video and the like can't be shown inside another app (content protection): use your phone's split screen, and control the music from the Click (Settings → Music).

video.howWeb: From YouTube: open the video, tap Share → Copy link, come back here and tap Paste link.

video.refSpeed: Speed the video was filmed at:
video.ytError: YouTube doesn't allow this video to be shown here (error {code}). Try another one.
watch.apple.step1: You need watchOS 10 or newer. On the Apple Watch look in Settings for Bluetooth cycling sensors (power and cadence).
watch.apple.step2: Pick Spindro when it appears and confirm.
watch.apple.step3: Start the Indoor Cycle workout from the Workout app: power and cadence should appear.
watch.aria: Watch: hold the top-left button, then choose Phone
watch.brand.intro: First open the Android app and turn broadcasting on (Garmin section). Your watch will see a sensor called "Spindro".
watch.brand.label: Brand
watch.brand.title: Your watch or bike computer
watch.brand.untested: It should work, but we haven't tried it on this watch. Whether it works or not, tell us with "Report a problem" below.
watch.coros.step1: On the watch go to System → Accessories and choose to add a Bluetooth accessory.
watch.coros.step2: Pick Spindro from the list. You can use it as a power meter.
watch.coros.step3: Start the Indoor Bike activity and wait for the accessory icon to stay solid, then press start.
watch.missing: Can't see the Phone icon? Add it in Settings → Controls on your watch.
watch.polar.step1: On the watch go to General settings → Pair and sync → Pair new device.
watch.polar.step2: Pick Spindro when it appears. You need a Polar watch that supports Bluetooth power sensors (not ANT+ only).
watch.polar.step3: Start an indoor cycling sport profile and check that power and cadence show up.
watch.step1: On {name} hold the LIGHT button (top left) to open the controls.
watch.step3: The phone shows as disconnected: now {name} can pair with "Spindro". When you finish, repeat the same gesture to reconnect it and sync.
watch.suunto.step1: On the watch open the sensors / connected devices settings and search for a new sensor.
watch.suunto.step2: Add Spindro as a power sensor (Power POD). Don't also add a bike sensor: cadence would come from that one.
watch.suunto.step3: Start the Indoor cycling activity: you should receive power and cadence.
watch.wahoo.step1: On the Elemnt open the menu and choose Add Sensor.
watch.wahoo.step2: Keep the phone close and pick Spindro when it appears. Save it.
watch.wahoo.step3: Start an indoor bike profile: you should see power and cadence.
welcome.step1: Turn on Bluetooth and wake your trainer by pedalling
welcome.step2: Tap the button below and pick your trainer
welcome.step3: Press Start and pedal: − and + change gear
welcome.subtitle: Three steps and you're riding.
welcome.title: Ready to ride?

Delete all data?

Your history, records, settings, workouts you created and the Strava link will be erased from this device. This cannot be undone.
wipe.hint: Removes your history, records, settings, workouts you created and the Strava link from this device. This cannot be undone: export your data first if you need it.
workout.connectHint: Connect your trainer: the workout starts anyway
workout.ftpFound: Best minute: {best} W. Your estimated FTP is {ftp} W (was {old} W). Save it?
workout.testTooShort: Test too short to estimate your FTP
workouts.accensione.desc: Short bursts to wake up your legs before a hard session. You finish breathing harder, but still in control.
workouts.accensione.name: Spark
workouts.cadenzalta.desc: Two minutes of fast, light pedaling, then a minute off, six times. Builds leg agility: your legs stay loose even as your breathing rises.
workouts.cadenzalta.name: High cadence
workouts.cadenzevar.desc: Six 2.5-minute blocks at a moderate load, each at a different cadence from 70 to 110 rpm. Builds control of your pedal rhythm: changing cadence without changing effort is harder than it looks.
workouts.cadenzevar.name: Variable cadence
workouts.cinquedatre.desc: Five three-minute efforts above threshold with two minutes of recovery. Builds aerobic power: breathing climbs hard and legs burn, but each effort stays the same.
workouts.cinquedatre.name: Five by three
workouts.costante.desc: Half an hour at a regular, comfortable pace. It builds your aerobic base.
workouts.costante.name: Steady endurance
workouts.domenicalunga.desc: A 90-minute zone 2 ride, with the last part a little firmer. Builds endurance for long days: you finish tired but satisfied, not wrecked.
workouts.domenicalunga.name: Long Sunday
workouts.doppiasoglia.desc: Two twenty-minute blocks just under threshold, with seven minutes between. Builds long threshold strength: it's hard and your breath gets heavy, but you can hold the pace to the end.
workouts.doppiasoglia.name: Double threshold
workouts.facile.desc: Light, steady pedaling. You can chat without effort: it builds the habit and helps you recover.
workouts.facile.name: Easy spin
workouts.fitHint: Copy it to your watch in GARMIN/NewFiles (USB) or import it into intervals.icu
workouts.fondo.desc: Aerobic endurance: the base of everything. Conversation pace.
workouts.fondo.name: Easy endurance
workouts.fondoprogr.desc: Four ten-minute steps, each a bit harder, up to a committed but sustainable pace. Trains control: you finish with full legs and a clear head.
workouts.fondoprogr.name: Progressive endurance
workouts.fondostabile.desc: Almost an hour in zone 2 at a steady, relaxed load. Builds the aerobic base: you can chat easily and the pace never changes.
workouts.fondostabile.name: Steady base
workouts.heading: Workouts
workouts.intro: The trainer sets the watts for each step from your FTP (200 W — change it in Settings or with the test). During a workout, + and − raise or lower the intensity by 5%.
workouts.lampi.desc: Thirty seconds hard and thirty easy, repeated. Builds aerobic power: near the end your legs burn while your breathing stays high.
workouts.lampi.name: Flashes 30/30
workouts.lungo60.desc: One hour at chatting pace. The heart of winter: lots of base, little strain.
workouts.lungo60.name: Long endurance 60
workouts.lungo75.desc: An hour and a quarter at an easy pace. Keep the watts steady and drink.
workouts.lungo75.name: Long endurance 75
workouts.lungo90.desc: An hour and a half at an easy pace. The long ride of the week.
workouts.lungo90.name: Long endurance 90
workouts.ottominuti.desc: Eight one-minute all-out efforts, each followed by an easy minute. Builds peak power: the last efforts hurt, and that is exactly where you improve.
workouts.ottominuti.name: Eight one-minutes
workouts.overunder.desc: Two blocks of three rounds: four minutes just under threshold, then one minute above. Trains a changing pace, like on hills and sprints: your legs learn to react without losing control.
workouts.overunder.name: Over and under
workouts.piramide.desc: Go up and down in intensity: 1-2-3-4-3-2-1 minutes, equal recoveries.
workouts.piramide.name: Pyramid
workouts.piramidecorta.desc: Five steps from 1 to 3 minutes just above threshold, with short recoveries. Trains holding a hard effort: the higher it climbs, the calmer your head has to stay.
workouts.piramidecorta.name: Short pyramid
workouts.ramp.desc: Start easy and every minute add 20 W until you can't hold on. Your FTP = 75% of your best minute. Stop pedaling (or press End) when you're at your limit.
workouts.ramp.name: Ramp FTP test
workouts.recuperoattivo.desc: Slow, easy spinning to flush out fatigue without adding more. You finish feeling lighter, like after a walk.
workouts.recuperoattivo.name: Active recovery
workouts.sblocco.desc: Light legs with a few short accelerations. Ideal the day after a hard effort.
workouts.sblocco.name: Openers
workouts.scalasoglia.desc: Seven steps that climb to full threshold and then back down, with two minutes of rest between them. Varied threshold work: the top step is tough, and the way down helps you hold on.
workouts.scalasoglia.name: Threshold ladder
workouts.seiscatti.desc: Six 15-second all-out sprints with four minutes of rest between them. Builds explosive power: the first sprints feel easy, the last ones really count.
workouts.seiscatti.name: Six sprints
workouts.soglia.desc: Two efforts at your FTP. Raises the ceiling of your sustainable power.
workouts.soglia.name: Threshold 2×15
workouts.sweet.desc: Three blocks just below threshold: the best trade-off between effort and progress.
workouts.sweet.name: Sweet spot 3×10
workouts.sweetcrescente.desc: Three ten-minute blocks, each a bit harder than the last, with five minutes of recovery. Builds threshold fitness without too much strain: breathing is full and the pace holds.
workouts.sweetcrescente.name: Sweet spot build
workouts.tempo.desc: Two blocks at a firm but controlled pace. You train to hold a brisk speed for longer.
workouts.tempo.name: Tempo 2×12
workouts.tempolungo.desc: Three fifteen-minute blocks just below threshold, with five easy minutes between. Builds endurance at a steady middle pace: demanding, but you can hold it with steady breathing.
workouts.tempolungo.name: Long tempo
workouts.title: Workouts and routes
workouts.trenta.desc: 2 sets of 8 × 30 seconds hard and 30 easy. Short but intense.
workouts.unagamba.desc: Single-leg pedaling at a light load to make the stroke rounder. It feels clumsy at first, then smoother; stop if you lose your balance.
workouts.unagamba.name: One leg at a time
workouts.ventidieci.desc: Three sets of eight rounds: twenty seconds all out, ten easy. Trains anaerobic power: your heart rate jumps fast and legs feel heavy, but the rounds stay short and manageable.
workouts.ventidieci.name: Twenty and ten
workouts.vo2.desc: Short, hard intervals to enlarge the engine.
workouts.vo2.name: VO2max 5×3
workouts.zona2allunghi.desc: An hour in zone 2 with five short surges above easy pace. Builds your base and your recovery: after each surge your breathing settles quickly.
workouts.zona2allunghi.name: Zone 2 with surges
workouts.zwoHint: Import it into intervals.icu, TrainingPeaks or Zwift
